newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice rates seen rising on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice rates seen rising on foreign buying.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to rise sharply next week amid foreign buying, dealers said on Thursday.

Prices of IRRI-6 variety rice rose to $215/225 per tonne FOB from $205/210 after the state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan (TCP) sold 36,000 tonnes to Mauritius on Wednesday, exporter Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said.
One official of the TCP said rice would be exported in four parcels between March 1997 and March 1998.

The first parcel of 12,000 tonnes at $235 per tonne FOB would be shipped in March/April, the second of 8,000 tonnes at $249 in May/June, the third of 8,000 tonnes at $249 in October/November and the fourth of 8,000 tonnes at $240 in March 1998, the official said.
In addition to IRRI-6, Mauritius was likely to buy superior quality basmati variety rice, Ghori said.
Prices rose sharply on Wednesday after domestic dealers and exporters got the news of Mauritius buying, Ghori said. "I think prices are likely to rise further," he added.
One official of the state-run Rice Export Corp of Pakistan (RECP) said prices were also likely to move up as several foreign buyers plan to buy from Pakistan.
A TCP official said Philippines had shown interest in buying rice from Pakistan but had not given any specific proposal. He said Pakistan was ready to sell to the Philippines.
A report from Manila said on Wednesday the Philippines' state-owned National Food Authority had signed a contract to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from Malaysia at $291.50 per tonne C&F.
Rice exports fell 40.09 percent to 139,132 tonnes worth $41 million in January from 232,231 tonnes worth $56 million in December.
In the first seven months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), rice exports rose 14.69 percent to 808,453 tonnes worth $237 million, compared to 704,880 tonnes worth $238 million in the year-ago period.
